completed_task_notes.NEX-039: The first real DecisionProvider adapter, so decisioning stops being a capability the platform can exercise but never use. Product commit 8e670a6, CI 4/4 completed/success at that exact SHA (polled 2026-11-25T19:32Z). Four refusals carry the security argument: a vendor cannot abstain (no 'abstained' outcome on the wire; the caller's threshold decides), the request carries only kind plus sorted candidates (no context hash, no excluded field names, no correlation id), sorting makes order-independence a property of this adapter rather than a hoped-for vendor trait, and a bad answer is an abstention rather than an exception. Construction fails closed on a non-https endpoint or an unbounded name. Two honest limits are recorded in the module docstring: the response size bound is enforced after httpx has read the body, and a rationale is truncated rather than treated as fatal.

run_summary: Implemented NEX-054. The redaction obligation previously had no adapter, so a policy that said 'allow with redaction' was refused outright. The shape-based credential judgement moved from bootstrap/logging_config.py into domain/redaction.py so the log formatter and the tool gateway share one implementation instead of drifting copies; the formatter re-exports it so no importer changed. InvokeTool now filters the tool result when a redaction obligation is present, on both the direct and the approval-gated path, and records an audit outcome that says redaction fired without naming the withheld fields. Filtering happens on the way out only, so the stored note is untouched. Unenforceable obligations still refuse the whole call. The run also found and corrected a run-integrity problem: it began on main instead of the authorized branch, so the gates were re-run on the feature-branch tree before the commit was made.
